title: Chat timeout_s never reaches HTTP client

answer.patch:
--- a/chat/wrap.py
+++ b/chat/wrap.py
@@ -16,12 +16,12 @@
     max_tokens: int = 1024,
     retry: int = 1,
 ) -> dict[str, Any]:
-    del timeout_s
     last: dict[str, Any] | None = None
     for _ in range(max(1, retry)):
         last = api.post_chat(
             model,
             messages,
+            timeout_s=timeout_s,
             temperature=temperature,
             max_tokens=max_tokens,
         )
answer.reason: In chat/wrap.py, the `chat_wrapped` function receives `timeout_s` as a parameter but immediately deletes it with `del timeout_s` (line 19) and never passes it to `api.post_chat`. The `api.post_chat` function has a default of `timeout_s=None`, so the HTTP layer always sees `None`. The fix removes the `del timeout_s` and passes `timeout_s=timeout_s` to `api.post_chat`.

title: Timed-out child with stderr-only output loses diagnostics

answer.patch:
--- a/util/subprocess_timeout.py
+++ b/util/subprocess_timeout.py
@@ -57,7 +57,7 @@
         stdout = e.stdout if e.stdout else ""
         stderr = e.stderr if e.stderr else ""
-        if str(stdout).strip():
+        if str(stdout).strip() or str(stderr).strip():
             return subprocess.CompletedProcess(
                 args=cmd,
                 returncode=-9,
answer.reason: The timeout handler on line 59 only checks `str(stdout).strip()` before returning a CompletedProcess with the captured output. When a subprocess writes only to stderr (e.g. progress messages) and then hangs, stdout is empty, so the condition is False and the code falls through to raise ProcTimeout — callers never see the stderr dump. Changing the condition to also check stderr ensures a CompletedProcess is returned whenever either stream has content.

title: Warmup ignores short timeout

answer.patch:
--- a/warmup.py
+++ b/warmup.py
@@ -9,5 +9,5 @@
 
 
 def warmup(model: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
-    _ = config.FIRST_BYTE_S
-    return chat(model, "Reply with exactly: OK")
+    return chat(model, "Reply with exactly: OK", timeout_s=config.DEFAULT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S)
--- a/chat/wrap.py
+++ b/chat/wrap.py
@@ -16,7 +16,6 @@
     max_tokens: int = 1024,
     retry: int = 1,
 ) -> dict[str, Any]:
-    del timeout_s
     last: dict[str, Any] | None = None
     for _ in range(max(1, retry)):
         last = api.post_chat(
answer.reason: warmup.py did not pass a short timeout to chat(), and wrap.py deleted the timeout_s parameter entirely, so the warmup path inherited the suite's FIRST_BYTE_S budget (600s) instead of failing fast with DEFAULT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S (30s). Two changes: (1) warmup.py now passes timeout_s=config.DEFAULT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S, and (2) wrap.py no longer deletes timeout_s so it propagates to the API layer.
